title: Is the cheap TV box worth it?
source: Matt's brief; Canadian prices checked October 2026 via news and provider sites; legal context from the 2019 GoldTV Federal Court order. Not legal advice.

beats.say: Will the cheap TV box just work, the way Telus TV does? ... Short answer, not quite. ... It saves real money, but it comes with catches.

slide.label: The cheap TV box
slide.title: Will it just work, like Telus TV?
slide.lede: A Firestick plus a live-TV service: about $150–400 a year after a one-time box. The savings are real. So are the catches.

beats.say: Before, TV cost about two thousand dollars a year. ... Telus was nine hundred, Sportsnet plus alone is three fifty, and the other subscriptions are roughly seven fifty. ... With Telus gone, that's about eleven hundred.

slide.label: What TV costs a year now
slide.title: Before: about *$2,000*

rows.label: Everything else: Apple One, Netflix, Prime…

slide.total: With Telus gone: about $1,100 a year.

beats.say: Here are four ways forward, in yearly costs. ... Keep everything as is, about eleven hundred. ... The box service plus the other subscriptions, around a thousand. ... The box service alone, one fifty to four hundred. ... Or trim and use Plex, about six hundred and twenty. ... The box itself is a one-time purchase on top, roughly fifty to a hundred dollars.

slide.label: Four ways forward
slide.title: What each one costs a year
slide.small: Estimates: everything else ~$750 (from the ~$2,000 total); trimmed = half dropped. Check the real bundle price.

beats.say: The appeal is easy to see. ... It's cheaper than cable, with a huge number of channels. ... Setup is simple, and trials or monthly plans cap the risk. ... A coworker vouches for it, though that's one person.

slide.label: The upside
slide.title: Why it's tempting

items.head: Big saving
items.sub: Often well under cable or Telus TV.

items.head: Lots of channels
items.sub: Live sports, news, movies. Count unverified.

items.head: Easy to start
items.sub: Arrives as a plug-in Firestick.

items.head: Low-risk trial
items.sub: Trials and monthly plans cap the cost.

slide.total: A coworker uses it and vouches for it. That counts, but it's one user.

beats.say: But it isn't Telus. ... This is a reseller of streams the channels never licensed, so it can vanish mid-term with no refund. ... Expect buffering at peak times like hockey night, possible blocking by your internet company, and no way to dispute an e-transfer.

slide.label: Will it just work?
slide.title: Not like Telus TV
slide.lede: Telus is a company with a phone number. This is a reseller of streams the channels never licensed.

items.head: It can vanish
items.sub: Mid-term, with no refund (unverified).

items.head: Peak-hour buffering
items.sub: Hockey night is when it strains.

items.head: Sites get blocked
items.sub: An internet-company block may need a VPN.

items.head: No money back
items.sub: E-transfer has no chargeback.

slide.small: Plus payment details go to a seller no one holds accountable.

beats.say: Tech support lands on you. ... Help is one person on WhatsApp. ... Apps are side-loaded, there are no profiles, and fifteen thousand channels are hard to dig through. ... Expect a few calls a month, and some outages.

slide.label: Who fixes it?
slide.title: You are tech support
slide.lede: Telus fixed problems. Here the only help is one person on WhatsApp.

items.head: It breaks at the worst time
items.sub: Game night, and the call comes to you.

items.head: No Netflix-style app
items.sub: No profiles; 15,000 channels to dig through.

items.head: Side-loaded apps
items.sub: Outside the app store; malware risk.

items.head: Nothing is checked
items.sub: Age, refunds, channel count: unverified.

slide.total: Expect a few calls a month, and some outages.

beats.say: What about watching the game later? ... Your dad often does that, and Telus records it on the PVR. ... This service lists a catch-up feature, but only on the premium plans, with no number of days given. ... It doesn't mention recording at all. ... It also never names hockey, baseball or football. ... So use the free trial to test all three before paying. ... And the ten day money-back promise covers monthly plans only, not yearly.

slide.label: Watching it later
slide.title: Can he watch it later?
slide.lede: Telus records games on the PVR. The Firestick Guy site is thinner on this.

items.head: Catch-up: premium plans only
items.sub: The site gives no number of days.

items.head: Recording: not mentioned
items.sub: No PVR to fall back on.

items.head: No sports named
items.sub: Hockey, baseball, football aren't listed.

items.head: Refund: monthly only
items.sub: The 10-day promise skips yearly plans.

slide.total: Use the free trial to test replay and hockey before paying.

beats.say: Plex is the free option worth knowing. ... Hundreds of live channels, tens of thousands of free movies and shows, with ads, plus some Canadian channels. ... It runs on most TVs, but there's no NHL.

slide.label: The free one
slide.title: Plex: *free*, with ads
slide.lede: Not cable, but a lot of watching for $0.

items.head: Live channels
items.sub: Hundreds: news, movies, kids, some sports.

items.head: On-demand library
items.sub: Tens of thousands of movies and shows.

items.head: Canadian channels
items.sub: Bell Media's CTV News and TSN The Ocho.

items.head: Runs on your TV
items.sub: App for Fire TV, Roku and most smart TVs.

slide.small: No NHL or premium cable channels. Channel counts vary by source (about 250–600+); check Plex's guide.

beats.say: So, trim first. ... Add Plex, pay for hockey only in season, and drop overlapping subscriptions. ... That gets close to six hundred twenty a year. ... If the box is still tempting, pay month to month, and keep another way to watch hockey in case it stops working.

slide.label: The takeaway
slide.title: Trim first, then decide
items: Pay for hockey only in season
That alone gets near *$620 a year*
total: Still tempted by the box? Pay month to month, not for a year.
Keep another way to watch hockey in case it stops working.
